```{r}
library(parameters)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
load("data/FEVdata.Rdata")
head(FEVdata)
```

```{r}
table(FEVdata$smoke)
table(FEVdata$sex)
FEVdata$smoke <- relevel(FEVdata$smoke, ref = "non-current smoker")
FEVdata$sex <- relevel(FEVdata$sex, ref = "male")
table(FEVdata$smoke)
table(FEVdata$sex)
```

```{r}
FEVdata$age_centered <- FEVdata$age - 10
FEVdata$height_centered <- FEVdata$height - 61
head(FEVdata)
```

```{r}
table(FEVdata$district)
prop.table(table(FEVdata$district))
```
FEV and district
```{r}
boxplot(FEVdata$fev ~ FEVdata$district)
```

Define model

Define three dummy variables for district, write linear equation as sum of the coefficients times the dummy variables 

```{r}
model_district <- lm(fev ~ district, data=FEVdata)
summary(model_district)
model_parameters(model_district)
```
p-values

- focus on individual dummy variables assocation with FEV, not the variable "district" as a whole
- want to assess against null that they are all 0
- use F-test, comes out of summary 
```{r}
summary(model_district)

# Or, equivalently, using the anova command (for testing nested models):
model_null <- lm(fev ~ 1, data=FEVdata)
anova(model_null, model_district)
```

Relationship between FEV and both age and smoking status

Define the model with age (centered) and smoking status as covariates
```{r}
model_multi <- lm(fev~ age_centered + smoke, data=FEVdata)
summary(model_multi)
```
Intercept is expected FEV for 10 year olds non-smokers
0.23 for age coefficient means FEV increases by 0.23 per year increase in age among people with the same smoking status. 
Estimated regression coefficent for smoking -0.21, so among people of the same age expect those exposed to smoke to have an FEV of 0.21 less than non-smokers 

smokers in red, non-smokers in blue 
```{r}
pred<-predict(model_multi, newdata=FEVdata)
plot(FEVdata$age_centered, FEVdata$fev)
lines(FEVdata$age_centered[FEVdata$smoke=="non-current smoker"], pred[FEVdata$smoke=="non-current smoker"], col="blue")
lines(FEVdata$age_centered[FEVdata$smoke=="current smoker"], pred[FEVdata$smoke=="current smoker"], col="red")
```

FEV of someone age 8 who doesn't smoke
```{r}
model_multi$coefficients[1]-2*model_multi$coefficients[2]
```

Age was likely a confounder between FEV and smoker status. 

Question 3

```{r}
plot(FEVdata$age_centered, FEVdata$fev)
```
Centered age and centered age squared as predictors 
```{r}
model_nonlin <- lm(fev ~ age_centered + I(age_centered^2) + I(age_centered^3), data=FEVdata)
model_parameters(model_nonlin)

# Plot FEV against centered age
plot(FEVdata$age_centered, FEVdata$fev)

# Add the fitted line (note: age has to be ordered for this plot)
lines(FEVdata$age_centered[order(FEVdata$age_centered)],    
      fitted(model_nonlin)[order(FEVdata$age_centered)],
      col = "red",  lwd = 2)

```
Testing nonlinearity: quadratic
```{r}
model_nonlinage <- lm(fev ~ age_centered + I(age_centered^2), data=FEVdata)
model_linage <- lm(fev ~ age_centered, data=FEVdata)
anova(model_linage, model_nonlinage)
```
Test for nonlinearity: cubic
```{r}
model_nonlinage <- lm(fev ~ age_centered + I(age_centered^2)  + I(age_centered^3), data=FEVdata)
model_linage <- lm(fev ~ age_centered, data=FEVdata)
anova(model_linage, model_nonlinage)
```
Null hypotheses are that beta2 =0 and/or beta3 =0, alternative is that they are not equal to 0. 

Question 4 interaction terms

Shorthand for writing out the interaction terms:
```{r}
model_interact <- lm(fev ~ age_centered*sex, data=FEVdata)
model_parameters(model_interact)
```
equivalent to:
```{r}
model_interact <- lm(fev ~ age_centered + sex + age_centered*sex, data=FEVdata)
model_parameters(model_interact)
```
- estimated change in FEV associated with one year increase in age is 0.27 for males and 0.16 for females. Estimated that females age 10 have a 0.33 lower FEV than males age 10.
Discrepancy exacerbates with age

```{r}
pred<-predict(model_interact, newdata=FEVdata)
plot(FEVdata$age_centered, FEVdata$fev)
lines(FEVdata$age_centered[FEVdata$sex=="male"], pred[FEVdata$sex=="male"], col="blue")
lines(FEVdata$age_centered[FEVdata$sex=="female"], pred[FEVdata$sex=="female"], col="red")
```

Binary/binary: smoke status and sex
```{r}
model_interact2 <- lm(fev ~ smoke*sex, data=FEVdata)
model_parameters(model_interact2)
```
Some evidence against the null hypothesis that no interaction between sex and smoke status. 
FEV for a male that smokes is 2.73+1.01, female who doesn't smoke = 2.73 -0.36, female who does smoke = 2.73+1.01 - 0.36 - 0.42 

Continuous/continuous:centered height and centered age and their interaction 

```{r}
model_interact3 <- lm(fev ~ age_centered*height_centered, data=FEVdata)
summary(model_interact3)
```
Evidence that the relationship between age and FEV does depend on height and vice versa. 

We see that for taller people, older age is associated with higher FEV (better lung funtion), but for shorter people, older age is associated with lower FEV (worse function).

We see that for younger people, an increase in 1-inch of height leads to a slightly higher expected FEV (slightly better lung function). For older people, an increase in 1-inch of height leads to a much greater expected FEV (better lung function).

Question 5: 
F-Test
```{r}
model_agesm <- lm(fev ~ age_centered + smoke, data=FEVdata) 
summary(model_agesm)
```
R-squared:

This means that the model explains 57.7% of the variation in FEV.
